newsitem.title: DUBAI: Asian envoys say some workers starving in UAE.
newsitem.headline: Asian envoys say some workers starving in UAE.

text.p: More than 100 Bangladeshis and Sri Lankans working at a United Arab Emirates garment factory are starving after employers cut off food rations and salaries, diplomats said on Monday.

"They are in hopeless conditions, they are starving and have not received salaries since May," A.M. Samsudeen, Sri Lankan ambassador to the UAE said of the 56 Sri Lankan workers at al-Tadaman Factory in the UAE emirate of Sharjah.
"There are 64 Bangladeshi workers at the same factory living in inhuman conditions," added a Bangladeshi diplomat.
The workers have not had their 400 dirham ($110) monthly salaries paid since May because of problems in management.
Recently they stopped getting daily meals and the factory is threatening to cut off water and electricity supplies to the camp housing them, diplomats said.
Most are surviving on food given to them by charities.
Company officials were not available for comment.
Local newspapers said the crisis has shed light on the need for stricter enforcement of regulations on minimum standards of accomodation, food and welfare for factory workers.
In two other textile factories, 241 Sri Lankans workers did not get their monthly salaries in over three months while 71 other compatriots had not had monthly wages since May.
The Sri Lankan and Bangladeshi envoys had raised the workers' plight with the UAE Labour Ministry undersecretary Isa al-Suweidi, who said he would take action, they added.

Samsudeen told Reuters he suggested to Suweidi that factory workers could be spared non-payment dues if a proposal to reintroduce a bank guarantee system for factories was approved. Suweidi promised to look into the matter, he added.
"In event of failure by the factory to pay wages to the workers, an equivalent amount will be deducted from the bank guarantee to pay them and their rights will be preserved," Samsudeen said.
Workers hope to be repatriated after they get their salaries and letter of release, diplomats said.

Hundreds of thousands of Asian workers have flocked to the oil-rich Gulf since the oil boom of the 1970s. Many of them live in labour camps where they get three meals a day, accomodation and a monthly salary.
